concepts.excerpt: The Avadhūta has just finished listing his twenty-four teachers — the earth, the wind, the fire, the ocean, a spider, a child, and the rest.

concepts.title: A King Asks a Naked Wanderer Why He Is Happy
concepts.excerpt: A king with everything meets a man with nothing who is visibly better off, and asks him to account for it.

concepts.title: The Question Put to Gorakhnāth at Kāmākhyā
concepts.excerpt: The whole of the eighty-four-lakh teaching comes out of a single evening, and the evening is described before anything is explained.

concepts.title: Eighty-Four Classrooms, Not Eighty-Four Sentences
concepts.excerpt: > ⚑ Cross-domain filing gate — the mechanism sentence.

concepts.title: Sādhanā Is the Last Stage
concepts.excerpt: The disciple is listening, and then one word brings him to a halt:

concepts.title: The First Circle — "I Must Live," and Not Yet "Why"
concepts.excerpt: A teacher draws six circles on the ground and makes the student stand in the first one.

concepts.title: As Long as Necessary
concepts.excerpt: The teacher draws a tree.

concepts.title: Sādhana Begins When the Reaction Becomes Observation
concepts.excerpt: You are at a yajña. The fire is going, the offerings are being made, and around the flame there are insects — coming in, circling, dropping into it.

concepts.title: The Bird Can Cross the Sky and Is Still Hungry
concepts.excerpt: Eleven lakh births are finished.

concepts.title: Emotion Is Not the Enemy — Emotion Is a Stage of the Consciousness
concepts.excerpt: Thirty lakh births, the largest circle in the whole scheme, and the definition that separates it from everything before is four short sentences:

concepts.title: You Enter the Human Birth by Asking Who Is Living It
concepts.excerpt: Eighty lakh classes of birth have been crossed. Four remain, and they are the human ones.

concepts.title: Six From the Guru, Three From the Teacher
concepts.excerpt: The list is running. Viveka, vicāra, saṅkalpa, vairāgya, bhāva, bhakti — six faculties of the human birth, delivered by the guru inside the story.

concepts.title: Four Conversions, Not One Renunciation
concepts.excerpt: Thirty lakh births in the animal circle, and what a person comes out holding is a set of feelings: attachment, fear, the instinct to protect what is theirs.

concepts.title: The Seventh Circle — From Bhoga to Bodha
concepts.excerpt: Go and talk to somebody who got everything. Not somebody comfortable — somebody who reached the top of the thing they were climbing, and is standing on it now.

concepts.title: Eighty-Four Classrooms, Not Eighty-Four Lakh Sentences
concepts.excerpt: Eighty-eight minutes of counted births end on a sentence that takes the counting away:

concepts.title: Tarpaṇa Refused on a Grievance — Settling Accounts With the Dead
concepts.excerpt: This material puts the objection in the practitioner's own mouth, in the words it apparently arrives in:

concepts.title: Sarpa-Doṣa Is an Imprint, Not an Event
concepts.excerpt: An astrologer looks at your chart and tells you there is a serpent problem in it.

concepts.title: One Pūjā Clears One Layer — and Karma Is Not Linear
concepts.excerpt: The passage opens by putting the listener's complaint into their own mouth, and it is the complaint of somebody who has already paid for this once:

concepts.title: The Debt Attaches to the Plot, Not to the Person Who Incurred It
concepts.excerpt: You did the ritual. A year ago, maybe two, maybe ten. You went south, you sat through it, you came home.

concepts.title: Two Tiers of Remedy — Including the Half That Costs Nothing
concepts.excerpt: The whole protocol is summarised in one sentence, and the verbs in it decide what kind of treatment this is:

concepts.title: Memory Without Knowledge, Time Without Urgency, Power Without Expression
concepts.excerpt: The realm gets four adjectives and they are the best description of it anywhere in the episode:

concepts.title: The Guardian Whose Trigger Condition Is Forgetting
concepts.excerpt: Most manifestation stories in this material begin with a demon or a petition.

concepts.title: The Consort He Says Is in No Book
concepts.excerpt: Something happens here that happens almost nowhere else in thirty-four sources.

concepts.title: Clean the Inside First, or Nothing You Offer Lands
concepts.excerpt: Most devotional advice tells you which deity to approach and what to bring.

concepts.title: Vāsuki, and the Rope That Was Pulled Both Ways
concepts.excerpt: Two teams take hold, one at each end. Gods on one side. Asuras on the other.

concepts.title: Be Still, and Hold a Steady World Inside You
concepts.excerpt: Seven of the eight nāgas teach by doing something — surrendering, striking, clarifying, refusing.

concepts.title: The Forest Was Burned, and the Bill Went to the Grandson
concepts.excerpt: Seven of the eight nāgas teach you something to do. The third one collects.

concepts.title: Mahāpadma: The Treasure-Keeper Whose Access Condition Is That You Stop Reaching
concepts.excerpt: The fourth of the eight serpent kings is described physically before anything is said about what he does:

concepts.title: Kulika: To Know the Light, the First Entrance Is Dark
concepts.excerpt: Eight serpent kings get named in this episode, each with a few sentences and a lesson, all of them attending the guardian of the serpent circle.

concepts.title: Karkoṭaka — The Poison That Turns Out to Have Been the Help
concepts.excerpt: The sixth of the eight serpent-kings gets fifty seconds, and the first thing said about him is what he does to people:

concepts.title: Padmanāga: Still the Water and You Can See Through It
concepts.excerpt: The seventh of the eight serpent kings gets two names, and both are unusually gentle for a roster that includes a snake of destiny who burns a king:

concepts.title: The Eighth One Only Ever Says *Not This*
concepts.excerpt: You're doing something — a job, a favour, a project you agreed to months ago — and partway through, something in you says no.

concepts.title: The Devī Acts Where Śiva Does Not
concepts.excerpt: There is a war on. Viṣṇu has sent the two brothers out, and they cannot be stopped.

concepts.title: The Dog on the Last Walk Is Bhairava's Own Awareness
concepts.excerpt: Four texts get named in one breath for what happens at death — a Yama Purāṇa, the Garuḍa Purāṇa, the Mahābhārata, and behind the whole episode the Kaṭha Upaniṣad.
